reference.title: Dates in lists and in order
reference.shortdesc: Where you can enter a date, how uFTi shows it, how it puts dates in order and what it checks.

section.title: Where you can enter a date

ul.li: The date of the event, in the Baptism, Birth, Burial and Death forms. The Event details form also has one.
The date of a marriage or other event, and the date of birth of each child, when you add a family.
The date of the census, in every census form. The 1939 register also asks for each person's date of birth.
The date of an event in a marriage register form.

section.p: A source has no date of its own. Give the date of a record to the event it is about.

section.title: How uFTi shows a date
section.p: A date is written in words, in the language of the app. It does not follow the date settings of your device. You will see 15 March 1900, March 1900 and 1900. An uncertain date reads about 1900, before 1900, after 1900, between 1850 and 1860 or from 1850 to 1860. A year before the common era reads 44 BC. A life span in a list reads 1816–1855.

section.title: How uFTi puts dates in order
section.p: uFTi orders by the year of the first date, as if that date were exact. It does not use the month or the day for an uncertain date.

table.title: How each kind of date is ordered

row.entry: The year 1900, both. Neither goes before or after it.
A year before the common era
It is not ordered by year, because uFTi reads no year in it.

section.p: On the page of a person, the events are in order of year, and then by the kind of event. The month and the day are not used. Events with no date come last. The family tree view uses the year, then the month, then the day, of the first date.

section.title: What uFTi checks
section.p: While you enter a date, uFTi checks that the day exists in that month and year of the calendar. It does not check that the events of one person are in a sensible order. Check yourself that a baptism comes after a birth, and a burial after a death.
Some forms warn you about a date but never stop you. A census form expects a Gregorian date on the day of the census.

section.title: Years before the common era
section.p: uFTi has no limit on the earliest year. Type BC or BCE after the year, such as 44 BC. The date pickers cannot enter these years, so you always type them.
